subject: Physics
title: Regular vs Diffused Reflection
summary: A mirror and a white wall both reflect light; only the mirror shows your face. Smooth surfaces keep rays parallel; rough ones scatter them.
keyPoints: **Smooth** surface → parallel rays stay parallel → image: **regular reflection**.
**Rough** surface → rays scatter → no image: **diffused reflection**.
Each ray still obeys **i = r** at its own tiny facet.
Diffused reflection lets us see a book from any angle; a wet road becomes smoother and glares.

blocks.alt: Parallel rays reflecting parallel from a smooth surface and scattering from a rough one
blocks.caption: Same laws, different surfaces.

quiz.q: A white wall shows no image because:
options: its rough surface scatters the rays
it breaks the laws of reflection
quiz.explain: Diffused reflection scatters the rays, so no image forms.

quiz.q: Does diffused reflection obey the laws of reflection?
options: Yes, at every tiny part of the surface
quiz.explain: The normals point different ways, but i = r holds at each point.

quiz.q: A wet road at night looks shiny because water:
options: fills the bumps and makes the surface smoother
quiz.explain: A smoother surface reflects more regularly, causing glare.

simulation.reason: A roughness slider shows the cause and effect directly: the same parallel rays scatter more as the surface gets rougher, while each still obeys i = r.
simulation.objective: See how surface roughness turns regular reflection into diffused reflection.
instructions: Increase the roughness and watch the reflected rays spread.
Check the readout: every ray still has i = r.
